title: Cloud: Provide a count API for each object type
description: We are providing new apis for developers to get total count of each collection. Currently you can obtain the total count from the total_results in meta field returned by each query method. However, with the rework of range based pagination. the query method's total_results will be limited to 5000. So we need to provide a different api for developers to obtain the total count. description: Add a new parameter """"content_type"""" for api: custom_mailer/email_from_template.json on the page http://docs.appcelerator.com/cloud/latest/#!/api/Emails    New Parameter:  1. content_type : String , it is an optional parameter.    Because one email template is able to have two formats email body: html and plain text. The parameter content_type can specify the email's format, valid value is """"html"""", """"plain"""" or """"multipart"""".  If the parameter content_type is not provided:  - will send """"multipart"""" format email if the email template has both html and plain text body.  - will send """"html"""" format email if the email template has only html body.  - will send """"plain"""" format email if the email template has only plain body.    If the parameter content_type is provided:  - will send specified type of email.  - if content_type is """"html"""", then it requires the email template must have html format body.  - if content_type is """"plain"""", then it requires the email template must have plain text body.  - if content_type is """"multipart"""", then it requires the email template must have both html and plain text body.    2. from_name: String, it is an optional parameter, this parameter is special for MessageGears delivery channel.  The """"from name"""" value. This header is supported by most email clients and displays in place of (or sometime along with) the “from email address” in the recipients email reader. About this parameter from_name, please refer to MessageGears documentation: http://docs.messagegears.com/docs/web-services/transactionaljobsubmit too. description: From 1.1.7 ACS will have a new ACL security behavior.  Currently all ACS objects has no default ACL, which any user can access any data which is not under ACL.  After 1.1.7, there will be a new app setting 'security' to enable the new security level 1, which for new app will still default to use the old security level -1(internally null).    User can manually set their security level 1 or -1 by using apps/update.json. Which now takes new parameter 'security' and value must be 1 or -1 in string.    When app's security level is 1(new), and object is created without assigning an ACL it will default to set its acl(acl_id) as the owner of object(user_id). Which should be only readable/writable to the owner.    When app's security level is changed -1(old) to 1(new), all those objects without ACL will remain as it is. Only the objects created after app's security is updated to 1 will be affective to use the new behavior. Those objects which using the old behavior should be public.    Queries on objects with ACL will have updates as well.  Apps with security level -1:  Should act same as before.  Apps with security level 1:  Query will only return objects which is readable by current session. Admin should be able to see any objects.    Also need to document that a user cannot be in more than 1000 ACL(https://jira.appcelerator.org/browse/CLOUDSRV-4496), and its readers list(internally r_ids field). Since when <objects>/query occurs, we will fetch ACLs which is readable by current user and this internally query on ACL will have a limit of 1000.
